Article Title: Nitin Gadkari says India is sending Rs 22 lakh crore out of country to import petrol, diesel, and gas; pushes sugar mills to make compressed bio gas, bio-manure, and sustainable aviation fuel
Article Text:
According to Gadkari, making better use of sugarcane by-products could also improve returns for farmers. (Image for representative purpose only)

Make gas, ethanol, aviation fuel

Barrier free tolling to save fuel and costs

India imports most of the fuel it consumes - be it crude oil, LPG, or even LNG. Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari has said that India’s agriculture sector can help drive down imported costs of fossil fuels, while at the same time using a combination of futuristic technology and a forward-looking vision if it is to become economically sustainable and help drive prosperity in rural India.Addressing the National Efficiency Awards ceremony organised by the National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories, Gadkari recently said producing sugar alone is no longer economically sustainable in view of global market conditions and the higher cost of production in India.Gadkari has called on sugar mills to expand into value-added by-products, particularly compressed bio-gas (CBG), ethanol, bio-manure and sustainable aviation fuel."Instead of dumping waste into road embankments, if we convert it into gas - into CBG - our imports will decline. Understand this figure: Rs 22 lakh crore. We are sending Rs 22 lakh crore out of our country to import fossil fuels - petrol, diesel, and gas," Gadkari said according to ANI.He pointed out that India's sugar output is between 300 and 350 lakh tonnes, while domestic consumption ranges from 280 to 300 lakh tonnes.The resulting surplus has put pressure on sugar prices.At the same time, he said, countries such as Brazil have a significantly lower production cost, at Rs 23 per kg compared with India's Rs 33 to Rs 34 per kg."The future of plain sugar is mediocre at best. I won't mince words: diversifying into complementary by-products guarantees a strong future," the Minister said.According to Gadkari, making better use of sugarcane by-products could also improve returns for farmers. He said the additional value generated through these products could eventually enable sugar mills to pay farmers as much as Rs 6,000 per tonne of sugarcane, compared with the current Rs 4,000.Gadkari also underlined the scale of India's agricultural waste and its potential as a source of bio-energy.Punjab and Haryana alone generate around 220 lakh tonnes of paddy stubble, he said. Five tonnes of stubble can produce one tonne of CBG, which he described as a way to address stubble burning and air pollution while simultaneously creating wealth in rural areas."Technology has arrived, allowing us to produce CBG from stubble, bamboo, rice straw, bagasse, and Napier grass. The Government of India launched a dedicated scheme. Look at the numbers: 1,908 CBG plants have been registered across the country, with 132 already operational," he said.India has the potential to produce 50,000 tonnes of CBG per day, Gadkari said, but present output accounts for only around two per cent of that capacity.The government has also introduced mandatory procurement obligations along with a fixed procurement price of Rs 106 per kg. He said the initiative could bring Rs 2.5 lakh crore into the rural economy and create as many as 15 lakh jobs.The Minister further called on the sugar industry to make greater use of artificial intelligence, precision farming and agricultural drones to reduce the cost of inputs and improve farm productivity.He cited the decision to permit ethanol production directly from corn as an example, saying the move had resulted in Rs 45,000 crore being transferred directly to farmers in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.Meanwhile, India is moving to a FASTag-enabled barrier-free tolling system which will not only save time, but also fuel costs.The government could gain an annual benefit of as much as Rs 25,000 crore once the electronic toll collection system FASTag is fully implemented, Gadkari said recently.Gadkari said the government is targeting the removal of barriers from all toll plazas on national highways by March 2027 as part of its plan to make toll collection completely barrier-free."When the system will go fully live, then our department alone would deliver a benefit of Rs 20,000-25,000 crore per year to the Government of India because of the use of FASTags," Gadkari said at the Global Fintech Fest.The minister said FASTag adoption has already resulted in a 10% increase in toll collections, translating into an additional Rs 7,000 crore approximately. Total revenue generated at toll booths has consequently risen to more than Rs 82,000 crore, according to Gadkari.
Article Summary: Gadkari has called on sugar mills to expand into value-added by-products, particularly compressed bio-gas (CBG), ethanol, bio-manure and sustainable aviation fuel. According to Gadkari, making better use of sugarcane by-product could also improve returns for farmers. India is moving to a FASTag-enabled barrier-free tolling system.

Article Title: Banks to open on Sunday ahead of 3-day nationwide strike: What customers should know
Article Text:
The government said it has taken the proactive steps to safeguard the banking needs of citizens. (AI image)

Also read:

Why are bank unions planning a strike?

NEW DELHI: Banks will remain open on Sunday, September 27, to ensure customers have access to essential banking services ahead of a proposed three-day nationwide strike, the government said on Wednesday.The move comes after the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) called for a nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With September 26 and 27 falling on a weekend, the strike could otherwise lead to an extended disruption in banking services, the govt said.“In view of the proposed three-day nationwide bank strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) from September 28 to 30, 2026, coinciding with the preceding weekend holidays of September 26 and 27, the government has taken proactive steps to safeguard the banking needs of citizens,” the finance ministry said in a statement.“In order to ensure that the genuine banking needs of the public are not adversely affected for an extended period, all Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks will function normally on Sunday, the 27th of September, 2026,” the ministry said.“The Department reiterates that the welfare and convenience of bank customers remains the Government's foremost priority. The Government and bank managements have appealed to unions to defer the proposed strike, and have also taken measures to ensure that essential banking services continue un-interrupted,” it added.The Reserve Bank of India has also approved the operation of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests on September 27.“Permission to operate Bank Branches and Currency Chests on Sunday, September 27, 2026. As requested in the above letter, with a view to ensuring that the genuine banking needs of the public are not adversely affected for an extended period, you have our approval for keeping the branches, offices, ATM link branches and Currency Chests of banks fully operational on Sunday, September 27, 2026," the apex bank said.“The banks may be advised to ensure adherence to relevant legal requirements in this regard. A list of Currency Chests of private sector/foreign banks has been sent to you separately,” it added.The UFBU has said bank operations could be disrupted across the country during the three-day strike from September 28 to 30. Since the strike follows the weekend holidays, customers could potentially face an effective five-day disruption in banking services.The timing is also significant as September 30 marks the half-yearly closing of banks, when reconciliation, provisioning, and treasury and market operations are carried out.The UFBU, which claims to represent around 90% of the banking workforce, has said it will proceed with the strike unless there is concrete progress on its key demand for five-day banking.“Responding to the appeal made by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Indian Banks' Association (IBA), Bank managements to defer the strike, we informed them that if there is any concrete and positive development towards implementation of our demand for introduction of 5 days banking, UFBU will consider the same,” the UFBU said in a statement following a meeting with the deputy chief labour commissioner.UFBU's other demands include an update and improvement of pension, a uniform dearness allowance formula for all pensioners and an option for employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS) to move to the old pension scheme (OPS). Bank unions under the UFBU had also gone on a nationwide strike on September 11 over their demands.The statement came after a conciliation meeting on Tuesday ended without a resolution. In the absence of such progress, the union said it would be “constrained” to go ahead with the proposed strike on September 28, 29 and 30.
Article Summary: The move comes after the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) called for a nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With September 26 and 27 falling on a weekend, the strike could otherwise lead to an extended disruption in banking services. The Reserve Bank of India has also approved the operation of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests.

Article Title: Oil prices slip 1% as traders hope for US-Iran truce amid fresh attacks on Saudi pipeline
Article Text:
Crude prices ease marginally on hopes of US-Iran truce

Oil prices eased marginally on Friday after a volatile week, as markets weighed hopes of a possible US-Iran truce against renewed risks to Saudi Arabia's oil infrastructure. WTI crude fell 1.09 points, or 1.15%, to $93.52 a barrel, while Brent crude declined 0.78 points, or 0.73%, to $105.80 a barrel, around 7:30 am IST.The declines followed a sharp rebound in the previous session. Both contracts had gained as much as 5% on Thursday, with Brent settling 3.4% higher and WTI up 2.7%. Brent's close was its highest since September 15, while the gain ended a six-session losing streak for WTI, during which it had fallen 13%.For the week, WTI was down 6.42%, while Brent was up 2.09%.Meanwhile, both the US and Iran are trying to work a potential route towards ending the Middle East conflict. Negotiators are discussing a phased path that would see Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lift its economic blockade of Iran, according to sources close to the talks.The Strait of Hormuz has remained central to concerns around energy supplies since the war began at the end of February. Around a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments have been curtailed since then, pushing prices 50% higher in March alone.The disruption has also led liquefied natural gas buyers to search further afield for new and stable supplies of the super-chilled fuel.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Thursday that the decision on ending the war rested with Washington."It's America that must choose whether it wants to end this or not," Pezeshkian said, responding to a question in an interview aired on Thursday on Fox News.At the same time, fresh military activity around Saudi Arabia has kept supply concerns in focus. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, preventing attacks on the southern province of Taif and the Yanbu area on the Red Sea.Saudi Arabia has been increasing crude pumping volumes through its East-West Pipeline to Yanbu, its Red Sea export hub. However, crude tanker loadings have not yet resumed, according to industry sources, satellite imagery and shipping data.The conflict is now nearing its seven-month mark, disrupting global oil trade and raising concerns over energy supplies.
Article Summary: WTI crude fell 1.15% to $93.52 a barrel, while Brent crude declined 0.73%. The declines followed a sharp rebound in the previous session. Both contracts had gained as much as 5% on Thursday, with Brent settling 3.4% higher.

Article Title: NSE IPO: Stock lists at Rs 1,800 versus issue price of Rs 1,785 on BSE with 0.8% premium; ends 1% up on first day
Article Text:
Before the IPO opened for subscription, NSE had raised Rs 6,746 crore from more than 150 anchor investors.

NSE Debuts on BSE, MSEI

NSE IPO GMP

NSE IPO listing date today: National Stock Exchange of India ’s shares debuted on the Bombay Stock Exchange at Rs 1,800 versus an issue price of Rs 1,785, marking a premium of around 0.8%. The stock closed its first trading session at Rs 1818, up 1% from its listing price, and 1.85% from its issue price.NSE made its stock market debut with a market capitalisation of more than Rs 4.45 lakh crore, becoming the second listed stock exchange in India. Its valuation at listing was significantly higher than that of rival BSE, whose current market capitalisation stands at Rs 1.33 lakh crore.Market participants were tracking grey market movements closely ahead of the listing, which is among the most anticipated market debuts of the year so far. Analysts said restrictions on exits by most large shareholders could limit the availability of NSE shares in the near term, potentially putting upward pressure on prices at a later stage.NSE's market debut gives investors an opportunity to assess how the exchange should be valued. Its longer-term growth outlook helped attract strong institutional interest, while retail investors appeared more cautious amid concerns about derivatives volumes, regulatory pressures and the possibility of more shares entering the market.Although investors remain broadly positive on NSE's longer-term prospects, the stock's performance in the months following its listing could depend on the amount of additional equity that becomes available once the lock-in periods for existing shareholders come to an end.In a circular issued on Wednesday, MSE said NSE's equity shares would be admitted for trading on its capital market segment under the ‘Permitted to trade’ category, effective September 24.The Metropolitan Stock Exchange is a Sebi-recognised national stock exchange that operates an electronic trading platform covering capital markets, equity derivatives, currency derivatives and debt segments. Its platform includes equity and index derivatives, debt and currency derivatives, with more than 250 listings and over 3,100 companies available for trading.The development comes days after NSE MD and CEO Ashish Chauhan made it clear that the exchange would not approach Sebi for permission to trade its own shares on its platform. Existing regulations of the market regulator do not permit a recognised stock exchange to list its own securities on its own trading platform.In the unlisted market, traders saw a grey market premium or GMP of around 2.2%. The stock has listed on a waek note with less than 1% premium over its issue price.The GMP was much higher earlier at Rs 250-310 a share, or roughly 14-17%. The steep decline had suggested expectations of only modest gains when the shares list."While investors have been waiting for the NSE listing for long, the enthusiasm has moderated because of the large issue size and expected supply," Abhay Doshi, co-founder of UnlistedArena.com told ET.At the IPO's upper price of Rs 1,785 per share, NSE's valuation stands at Rs 4.42 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.33 lakh crore for rival BSE. Some market participants said the balance between available supply and investor demand could play an important role in determining how NSE shares perform in the initial trading sessions after listing.The listing brings to an end NSE's long-running journey towards becoming a listed company and make it India's second listed stock exchange after BSE.NSE launched its initial public offering earlier this month, seeking to raise Rs 22,562 crore through a 12.64 crore-share offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders.Since the issue was entirely an OFS, NSE itself will not receive any money from the IPO. The proceeds will instead accrue to the shareholders selling their stakes through the offering.The IPO price band was fixed at Rs 1,700 to Rs 1,785 per share. With the lot size set at 8 shares, retail investors were required to invest a minimum of Rs 14,280 to apply for the issue.Before the IPO opened for subscription, NSE had raised Rs 6,746 crore from more than 150 anchor investors.Foreign portfolio investors made up Rs 2,883 crore, or 43%, of the total anchor book. The anchor round saw participation from more than 20 foreign long-only funds, including Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Norges Bank.Domestic institutional participation was similarly spread across investors. More than 25 mutual funds, along with 11 insurance and pension companies, invested around Rs 3,588 crore, accounting for 53% of the anchor book.LIC, which is NSE's largest shareholder with a 10.72% stake, also participated in the anchor round. LIC, LIC Mutual Fund and LIC Pension Fund together invested more than Rs 500 crore. The investment was made even though LIC's existing shareholding in NSE is larger than the stake being offered through the IPO.The SBI group also took part in the anchor book through SBI Mutual Fund, SBI General, SBI Life and SBI Pension Fund. State Bank of India and SBI Capital Markets are together selling a 1% stake in NSE, while the group's combined investment in the exchange through its various entities exceeds Rs 400 crore.NSE's first public issue attracted strong demand during the three-day subscription period from September 17 to September 21. The IPO was subscribed nearly six times the shares on offer. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) drove the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion around 13 times, while the portions allocated to retail investors and non-institutional investors (NII) were subscribed 1.4 times and 6.6 times, respectively.
Article Summary: NSE made its stock market debut with a market capitalisation of more than Rs 4.45 lakh crore, becoming the second listed stock exchange in India. The stock closed its first trading session at Rs 1818, up 1% from its listing price, and 1.85% from the issue price.

Article Title: Festive season shock: AC, TV and appliance prices set to rise from October 1
Article Text:
The latest increase comes ahead of the peak festive shopping period.

AC prices to rise 5-8%

Companies see more price hikes ahead

Haier plans multiple rounds of hikes

Festive demand faces a test

TV prices could see sharper increase

Consumers could face higher prices for air conditioners, washing machines, refrigerators and LED TVs this festive season, with leading appliance and consumer electronics makers planning price hikes of up to 8% from October 1 as rising commodity and freight costs squeeze margins.The latest increase comes ahead of the peak festive shopping period and marks the third round of price hikes by the industry in 2026.Manufacturers said sustained increases in copper, aluminium, steel and crude oil derivatives, along with higher freight costs and currency volatility linked to the West Asia crisis, have made further price revisions necessary.Air-conditioner prices are expected to rise by around 5-8%, while some manufacturers are raising prices of washing machines, refrigerators and LED TVs by 3-4%. Other companies are still assessing the impact of higher input costs, PTI reported.Companies including Blue Star, Godrej Appliances, Haier, Daikin and Super Plastronics have announced or confirmed price increases ranging from 4% to 10% across categories.LG and Bosch Home Comfort, which owns the Hitachi air-conditioner brand, have also increased AC prices by around 5%, according to PTI sources.Panasonic, meanwhile, is still evaluating the situation.Blue Star Managing Director B Thiagarajan said prices of ACs and deep freezers had already increased by 5-8% because of higher commodity costs."All the commodity prices have been going up because of the war. Copper, steel and plastics have all become costlier," he said, adding that this is the third price increase undertaken by the company this year.Compared with last year's festive season, Thiagarajan said costs have risen by around 15%. However, with GST benefits of about 10% now available to consumers, the net impact for buyers would be roughly 5%, he said.Kamal Nandi, Business Head and Executive Vice President, Appliances Business, Godrej Enterprises Group, said another industry-wide price increase had become ‘inevitable’ after commodity prices rose 8-10% since the previous revision."Price hikes of 5-7 per cent across categories will happen. The timing may differ from brand to brand, with some implementing it from October and others from November, but it has to happen," he said.Nandi, however, said consumers could still buy appliances at existing prices during the festive season because dealers and distributors had stocked products before the price increases."There are pipelines which will last for about a month to one-and-a-half months. Diwali should largely get covered with old-price inventory. Post-Diwali, the new prices will certainly take effect," he added.Haier India President NS Satish said the company had little choice but to raise prices as input costs continued to climb. "If we avoid taking price hikes, we will lose money. If we increase prices, sales may be slightly impacted, but there is no choice," he said.Haier plans to increase prices of room air conditioners by around 5% from October 1. It may undertake further increases after Diwali and again in January if input costs remain elevated.The company has also confirmed a 2-3% increase in prices of other products, including LED TVs and washing machines.Satish said copper prices had risen sharply over the past year, increasing manufacturing costs, particularly for air conditioners, where copper is a key component.He said Haier expects a cumulative price increase of around 15% between now and January — 5% from October, another 5% around December and a further 5% in January.Copper prices, which were around 8,000-9,000 per metric tonne last year, have now touched $14,500 and are expected to rise further, Satish said. An air conditioner typically requires around 3-4 kg of copper.The timing of the price increases is significant because the festive period from Onam through Dussehra and Diwali typically accounts for around 30-40% of annual sales for appliance manufacturers, according to sector reports.Daikin Airconditioning India Chairman and Managing Director Kanwaljeet Jawa said the company had already raised prices by 8-10% from September 16."Copper prices have gone up by almost 25-35 per cent. The dollar is strengthening and commodity prices continue to rise. Companies are under tremendous pressure," he said.Jawa said consumer demand remained strong for now but acknowledged that prolonged cost pressures could affect the market."I don't know what will happen going forward, but everybody is aware of the reality in the marketplace right now. It might affect things in the long term if the situation doesn't improve," he said.Super Plastronics Pvt Ltd, which manufactures and markets television brands including Thomson, Kodak and Blaupunkt in India, plans to increase TV prices by around 7% after October. Appliance prices have already risen by 4-5%, the company said.SPPL Director Avneet Singh Marwah said higher prices could weigh on festive demand, when consumers typically expect discounts and promotional offers."Global instability and rising costs will definitely have some impact on consumer sentiment," he said.Panasonic Life Solutions India Head of Product Marketing and Planning (AC category) Abhishek Verma said the company was monitoring market conditions before deciding on a price increase."The industry continues to witness unprecedented cost pressures and we are evaluating the situation carefully," he said.Videotex Director Arjun Bajaj said higher freight costs and supply-chain disruptions could establish a new pricing benchmark after Diwali."Television prices for smaller screen sizes could rise by up to 20 per cent, while larger screen sizes may see increases of up to 10 per cent, depending on screen size," he added.
Article Summary: Companies including Blue Star, Godrej Appliances, Haier, Daikin and Super Plastronics have announced or confirmed price increases ranging from 4% to 10% across categories. Manufacturers said sustained increases in copper, aluminium, steel and crude oil derivatives, along with higher freight costs and currency volatility linked to the West Asia crisis, have made further price revisions necessary.

Article Title: Mehli Mistry to leave Tata Med Centre Trust, his 6th such exit
Article Text:
MUMBAI:

Mehli Mistry, M Pallonji Group director and confidant of the late Ratan Tata , will not seek re-election as Tata Medical Centre Trust (TMCT) trustee when his term expires on Sept 30. This will make it his sixth exit from a Tata institution since Ratan Tata’s death in Oct 2024. Mehli sent an email to this effect to the board on September 15.He has served on TMCT board since 2017. His departure will leave the board to Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, his children Leah, Maya and Neville, and former defence secretary Vijay Singh. Singh’s term ends next year.The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust, which are locked in a governance dispute with the Tata Sons board, set up TMCT in 2005 to run Tata Medical Center hospital in Kolkata. It is the biggest hospital owned by the Trusts. The hospital generates enough funds to sustain itself and no longer requires fresh capital from SDTT and SRTT.Built at a cost of about Rs 700 crore on a 13-acre campus in New Town, the 600-bed cancer hospital is modelled on Mumbai’s Tata Memorial Centre and serves patients from eastern and northeastern India and neighbouring countries.SDTT had established the Tata Memorial Centre in Parel in 1942 for Rs 5 lakh and with 80 beds.After the hospital’s control shifted to the govt, it maintained limited ties primarily providing grants and representation on the council.The Kolkata hospital was previously overseen by Mehli until he invited Noel Tata onto the TMCT board in Oct-Nov 2024, after which responsibilities were transitioned to him.Mehli had exited SDTT and SRTT boards after his term was blocked by Noel Tata, Singh and Venu Srinivasan in Oct 2025, and has since stepped down from the National Centre for Performing Arts (NCPA) and the Small Animal Hospital in Mumbai.Mehli, however, continues on the board of Tata Education and Development Trust—the richest trust within Tata Trusts —where he is a lifelong trustee.The TMCT exit extends a pattern: Mehli’s retreat from institutions built around Ratan Tata’s personal legacy is accelerating as the succession fight over Tata Sons plays out in parallel.
Article Summary: Mehli Mistry will not seek re-election as Tata Medical Centre Trust (TMCT) trustee when his term expires on Sept 30. This will make it his sixth exit from a Tata institution since Ratan Tata’s death in Oct 2024. Mehli sent an email to this effect to the board on September 15.

Article Title: Market mood check: Crude, US-Iran talks and economic data to drive Dalal Street this week
Article Text:
Crude, US-Iran talks and key data in focus this week

Bond yields, rupee under watch

Economic data to provide market cues

US, eurozone data in focus

Dalal Street is likely to begin the holiday-shortened week with investors tracking a mix of geopolitical developments, oil prices and global financial conditions. According to analysts, developments in US-Iran diplomacy and movements in crude oil will be among the key factors determining market sentiment.The market is expected to remain cautious as geopolitical developments, crude oil prices and global bond yields continue to influence the near-term direction. Equity markets will remain closed on Friday for Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti."Globally, developments around US-Iran diplomacy and crude oil prices will remain critical. Any progress on a framework for reopening the Strait of Hormuz could ease energy prices and provide some relief to India's import bill and the rupee, while renewed geopolitical tensions could keep volatility elevated," Ajit Mishra, SVP, Research, Religare Broking, said.The direction of oil prices will therefore remain closely linked to developments in the US-Iran talks. Brent crude is currently near $105–106 a barrel, a level that analysts said continues to weigh on the macroeconomic outlook."Brent crude near $105–106 a barrel remains too elevated to provide meaningful macroeconomic relief. Progress in the US-Iran negotiations could help reduce the geopolitical premium in oil prices, while renewed escalation or supply disruptions could intensify inflationary pressures."The US 10-year treasury yield, currently near 5.2 per cent, will remain another important constraint on global risk appetite," Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder & CEO of HST Wealth, a research analyst firm, told PTI.Beyond crude oil, movements in global bond yields and the dollar will be another important factor for emerging markets following the Federal Reserve's September policy decision."Global bond yields will also remain important following the Federal Reserve's September policy decision. Further increases in yields and the dollar could weigh on emerging-market capital flows, while a moderation in yields could provide some relief."The rupee will remain another important factor to watch, with persistent oil-related demand for dollars and continued FII outflows potentially keeping the currency under pressure, although RBI intervention has helped contain excessive volatility," Ponmudi R, CEO - Enrich Money told PTI.Analysts said the combination of higher oil prices, elevated yields and geopolitical uncertainty had contributed to the sharp sell-off during the middle of last week. Ponmudi said elevated yields continued to tighten global financial conditions and could reduce the relative attractiveness of emerging-market assets.Foreign institutional investor activity will consequently remain on the radar, along with movements in the rupee and global risk sentiment.Investors will also have several domestic indicators to track during the week. August industrial production data and the HSBC manufacturing PMI reading are scheduled for release, while monthly auto sales figures will also be watched.Mishra said market participants would closely monitor these indicators alongside FII activity.Siddhartha Khemka, head of research, wealth management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said markets would also track India's August industrial production data and the federal fiscal deficit for cues on domestic momentum and the consolidation path.The global economic calendar will add another layer to the market outlook. A series of US economic data releases will be important for global risk sentiment, while US consumer confidence and JOLTS job openings will be watched for their implications for expectations around the global rate cycle.The eurozone's September inflation cluster will also be on the radar as investors assess the direction of the global rate cycle.The focus on global data comes after a weak performance at the Dalal Street last week. BSE benchmark Sensex declined 399.22 points, or 0.53 per cent, while NSE Nifty50 dipped 205.9 points, or 0.88 per cent.
Article Summary: Dalal Street likely to begin the holiday-shortened week with investors tracking a mix of geopolitical developments, oil prices and global financial conditions. Equity markets will remain closed on Friday for Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti. August industrial production data and the HSBC manufacturing PMI reading are scheduled for release.

Companies are under tremendous pressure," he said.Demand remains good for now, Jawa said, but added, "I don't know what will happen going forward, but everybody is aware of the reality in the marketplace right now. It might affect things in the long term if the situation doesn't improve."SPPL, which manufactures and markets Thomson, Kodak and Blaupunkt TVs in India, plans to increase TV prices by around 7% after October. Appliance prices have already risen 4-5%.SPPL Director Avneet Singh Marwah said higher prices could affect festive demand as consumers generally expect discounts and promotional offers."Global instability and rising costs will definitely have some impact on consumer sentiment," he said.Panasonic Life Solutions India head of product marketing and planning (AC category) Abhishek Verma said that the company was monitoring market conditions before deciding on any increase. "The industry continues to witness unprecedented cost pressures and we are evaluating the situation carefully," he said.Videotex director Arjun Bajaj said rising freight costs and supply chain disruptions were expected to create a new pricing benchmark after Diwali."Television prices for smaller screen sizes could rise by up to 20 per cent, while larger screen sizes may see increases of up to 10 per cent, depending on screen size," he said. With manufacturers facing sustained commodity and freight cost pressures, price increases are now being implemented across categories at different points between October and the post-Diwali period.
Article Summary: Leading manufacturers are raising prices by 5-8% from October 1. This will be the industry's third price hike in 2026. Some companies are increasing prices of washing machines, refrigerators and LED TVs by 3-4%. Others are still evaluating the impact.

Article Title: Banks open today: Are banks open or closed on Sunday, September 27, ahead of a 3-day strike?
Article Text:
All public sector banks and regional rural banks will remain operational on Sunday.

Are banks open today?

Why are bank unions going on strike?

NEW DELHI: Banks are open and functioning normally across the country on Sunday, September 27, as the government takes steps to ensure "uninterrupted banking services" ahead of the proposed three-day nationwide strike from September 28 to 30.The move comes as the strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) follows the weekend holidays on September 26 and 27. The decision is aimed at giving customers an additional working day and preventing an extended disruption in banking services.“In view of the proposed three-day nationwide bank strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) from September 28 to 30, 2026, coinciding with the preceding weekend holidays of September 26 and 27, the government has taken proactive steps to safeguard the banking needs of citizens,” the finance ministry said in a statement.“In order to ensure that the genuine banking needs of the public are not adversely affected for an extended period, all Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks will function normally on Sunday, the 27th of September, 2026,” the ministry added.The Reserve Bank of India has also approved the opening of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests on the day, allowing them to remain fully operational.Bank of India has separately approved the operation of its branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests on Sunday.“The Department reiterates that the welfare and convenience of bank customers remains the Government's foremost priority. The Government and bank managements have appealed to unions to defer the proposed strike, and have also taken measures to ensure that essential banking services continue un-interrupted,” the finance ministry said.The UFBU has called a nationwide strike from September 28 to 30, with five-day banking being its key demand. The unions have also sought improvements in pension benefits, a uniform dearness allowance formula for all pensioners and an option for employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS) to shift to the old pension scheme (OPS).The government has said it has already decided to keep the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme in abeyance following discussions with the unions. The demand for a five-day banking week is still under consideration.The UFBU had also held a nationwide strike on September 11 over its demands. The unions have said they could reconsider the proposed strike if there is concrete progress on the five-day banking demand.“Responding to the appeal made by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Indian Banks' Association (IBA), Bank managements to defer the strike, we informed them that if there is any concrete and positive development towards implementation of our demand for introduction of 5 days banking, UFBU will consider the same,” the UFBU said in a statement following a meeting with the deputy chief labour commissioner.A conciliation meeting earlier last week ended without a resolution. The UFBU said that in the absence of concrete progress, it would be “constrained” to go ahead with the proposed strike on September 28, 29 and 30.The timing of the proposed strike is significant because September 30 is the half-yearly closing of banks. The period involves key operations such as reconciliation, provisioning, treasury and market activities.With the strike following the September 26-27 weekend holidays, customers could otherwise face an extended disruption in banking services. Keeping banks open on Sunday is therefore aimed at providing customers with an additional working day before the strike begins.
Article Summary: All public sector banks and regional rural banks will remain operational on Sunday. The Reserve Bank of India has also approved the opening of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests. The move comes as the strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) follows the weekend holidays on September 26 and 27.

Article Title: GIFT Nifty breaks the $23 billion mark as trading activity hits a fresh high
Article Text:
GIFT Nifty breaks the $23 billion mark

GIFT Nifty's expansion since its full-scale launch in July 2023 has taken the international platform to another trading milestone, with turnover, volume and open interest all hitting fresh highs on September 25.The platform's cumulative turnover reached $3.52 trillion as of September 25, 2026, while more than 76.19 million contracts had been traded since the start of full-scale operations, NSE International Exchange (NSE IX) said in a press release.The latest session added another record to that growth. GIFT Nifty's turnover for the day stood at $23.67 billion, its highest-ever single-day figure, with 5,12,023 contracts changing hands.The platform also ended the session with its highest-ever open interest at $21.87 billion, equivalent to around Rs 2.10 lakh crore. The corresponding number of contracts stood at 4,71,287.Both figures moved past their previous records. The earlier single-day turnover high was $23.48 billion on February 20, 2026, while the previous open interest record of $21.56 billion was set on June 25, 2026.NSE IX described the latest milestones as a “new era for Gift Nifty”.It said trading turnover has been “growing exponentially” since the platform began full-scale operations on July 3, 2023.GIFT Nifty's record session came just a day after another major development involving the National Stock Exchange of India. NSE was listed on the BSE on September 24, with its shares making their debut at Rs 1,800 against an issue price of Rs 1,785. The listing price represented a 0.84 per cent premium.NSE is one of India's leading stock exchanges and provides trading across multiple asset classes. Its unique investor base crossed 11 crore in January 2025. The exchange also processed more than 2,000 crore orders in a single day on July 23, 2024, and around 29 crore trades on June 5, 2024. Both were described as the highest in the world.The international platform behind GIFT Nifty is NSE IX, which was established at GIFT City in 2017 as a multi-asset international exchange. Its offerings cover Indian single-stock and index derivatives, currency derivatives, depository receipts and global stocks.NSE IX also operates primary-market products covering equity shares, REITs, InvITs and debt securities.The exchange said GIFT Nifty and NSE IX have received regulatory exemptions that allow US customers to participate in derivative contracts listed on NSE IX. These exemptions support the platform's international participation.
Article Summary: GIFT Nifty's cumulative turnover reached $3.52 trillion as of September 25, 2026. More than 76.19 million contracts had been traded since the start of full- scale operations in July 2023. GIFT Nifty ended the session with its highest- ever open interest at $21.87 billion.

Article Title: NTPC, EDF Power Solutions India form joint venture for pumped storage; hydro and renewable energy projects
Article Text:
NTPC terminates Rs 413 crore Mouda BESS contract after contractor default

NEW DELHI: State-run National Thermal Power Corporation Limited has entered into a joint venture with French firm Électricité de France (EDF) Power Solutions India to jointly develop, own and operate pumped storage projects, hydropower projects, other renewable energy ventures, and distribution business.The 50:50 joint venture will take up projects both within India and in neighbouring countries, NTPC said in a statement.The agreement was inked on September 25, in the presence of NTPC chairman Gurdeep Singh and Bernard Fontana, chairman and CEO of EDF SA, France.EDF Power Solutions is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the French electricity major EDF (Électricité de France). Through this strategic tie-up, the two companies aim to set up a responsible and innovative industrial entity focused on developing, building and operating low-carbon power plants, along with flexibility solutions and transmission assets.NTPC and EDF will draw on their respective areas of expertise to offer customised solutions, aimed at driving the decarbonisation and overall performance of electrical systems. This aligns with India's ambitious target of achieving 100 GW of installed pumped storage capacity by 2036.Given their combined expertise and resources, both companies are expected to make a significant contribution to India's renewable energy sector, furthering innovation and environmental sustainability.
Article Summary: The 50:50 joint venture will take up projects both within India and in neighbouring countries. The agreement was inked on September 25, in the presence of NTPC chairman Gurdeep Singh and Bernard Fontana, chairman and CEO of EDF SA, France.

Article Title: India’s tourism boom: Sector adds 5.22% to GDP, supports 8.46 crore jobs
Article Text:
India's e-Visa facility, which covered nationals of 43 countries when it was introduced in 2014, has now expanded to 172 countries. Travellers can enter India using e-Visas through 88 international ports.

Tourism activity expands

Digital push

National Digital Tourism Stack

Connectivity boost

NEW DELHI: India’s tourism sector contributed 5.22 per cent to the country’s GDP and supported 8.46 crore jobs in 2023-24, as the government highlighted the sector’s growing economic role ahead of World Tourism Day on September 27. The government said the expansion of digital platforms and artificial intelligence is also reshaping how tourists discover, plan and experience destinations.World Tourism Day 2026 will be observed under the theme “Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism”, putting technology at the centre of discussions on the future of travel.India recorded 428.55 crore domestic tourist visits in 2025, sharply higher than 67.7 crore in 2021. Foreign tourist visits also rose to 2.53 crore in 2025, from 0.1 crore in 2021.The increase in tourist activity has also boosted foreign exchange earnings. Tourism-related foreign exchange earnings rose to Rs 2,76,831 crore in 2025, compared with Rs 63,978 crore in 2021.The government said digital tools are increasingly making travel more personalised, accessible and seamless.India's e-Visa facility, which covered nationals of 43 countries when it was introduced in 2014, has now expanded to 172 countries.Travellers can enter India using e-Visas through 88 international ports.Around 78 per cent of visas are now issued electronically, while about 95 per cent of e-Visa applications are processed within 72 hours, according to the government.The revamped Incredible India Digital Platform also offers virtual experiences covering cultural, heritage, adventure, gastronomical, wellness, art and craft, and rural attractions.Its AI-powered features include real-time weather updates, city exploration and access to travel services.The ministry of tourism is set to launch the National Digital Tourism Stack, an open digital public infrastructure initiative aimed at making tourism offerings more discoverable, accessible and trustworthy.The government will also roll out Dekho Apna Desh 2.0, which will promote lesser-known destinations and seek to distribute tourist footfall more evenly across the country.Alongside the digital push, the government is expanding physical tourism infrastructure.Under the Modified UDAN scheme for 2026-27 to 2035-36, an approved outlay of Rs 28,840 crore includes plans to develop 100 airports and 200 modern helipads.The initiative is aimed at improving air connectivity to tourism destinations and supporting the sector's wider expansion.
Article Summary: India recorded 428.55 crore domestic tourist visits in 2025, sharply higher than 67.7 crore in 2021. Tourism-related foreign exchange earnings rose to Rs 2,76,831 crore in 2025. India's e-Visa facility, which covered nationals of 43 countries in 2014, has now expanded to 172 countries.

Article Title: India to build 1st port-based Rs 2,300 crore e-methanol plant at Kandla to supply green fuel to ships
Article Text:
Port project greenlit

NEW DELHI: India is looking to turn its ports into green-fuel hubs as it moves to supply low-carbon fuel to international shipping, with a Rs 2,300-crore e-methanol plant being set up at Kandla in Gujarat.Union ports, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal said the project marked a shift towards India supplying the fuel that powers global maritime trade.“India moves up as the world's leading maritime power; it will now power the world's ships with green energy,” Sonowal said at the foundation stone ceremony on Saturday.The plant, being developed by Deendayal Port Authority (DPA) and Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd (APCL), will have a total production capacity of 150 tonnes per day. It will use renewable power, water and biogenic CO2 to make e-methanol, which will be supplied to vessels operating on the Asia-Europe International Trade Corridor.The project will be developed in two stages. The first 50-tonne-per-day unit, costing Rs 1,200 crore, is scheduled to be completed by January 2027. Another 100 tonnes per day will be added under the second phase at a cost of Rs 1,100 crore, with completion targeted for March 2027.The government said the plant is expected to produce green methanol at about $750 per tonne, compared with a global rate of around $1,300 per tonne. It is also expected to generate more than 3,500 direct and indirect jobs.DPA will own 76 per cent of the project and APCL the remaining 24 per cent. DPA's contribution includes Rs 567.32 crore in equity, 75 acres of land, desalinated water and renewable energy in the form of green hydrogen.The project also links India's maritime expansion with its broader decarbonisation plans. The government said it will contribute to the country's target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070, while supporting energy self-reliance and domestic manufacturing.The Kandla facility is part of a wider push to expand India's maritime capacity. The government plans to add 100 ships to the country's merchant fleet over the next five years and aims to make India one of the world's five largest ship-owning nations by 2047.Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel said the project would turn the state's renewable-energy potential into an export opportunity.“Kutch and the long coastline of Gujarat will now power the world's ships through Kandla,” Patel said, adding that the plant would make the Gujarat coast a gateway for India's green energy exports.The project also brings together DPA and APCL, which is based in Namrup, Assam. Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the partnership would connect the Northeast's energy potential with India's wider clean-energy ambitions.
Article Summary: India is looking to turn its ports into green-fuel hubs as it moves to supply low-carbon fuel to international shipping. A Rs 2,300-crore e-methanol plant is being set up at Kandla in Gujarat. Union ports, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal said the project marked a shift towards India supplying the fuel that powers global maritime trade.

Article Title: NACOF reports Rs 2,456 crore revenue, declares 12% dividend, plans international expansion
Article Text:
NACOF said it is exploring partnerships with cooperative systems and farming organisations in Bangladesh, Iran, Russia and Chile, along with opportunities in Dubai and other international markets.

The federation plans to use its cooperative network to establish business relationships and create opportunities for Indian cooperatives overseas.

NACOF plans international cooperative partnerships

Federation seeks action-oriented partnerships

NEW DELHI: The National Federation of Farmers' Procurement, Processing & Retailing Cooperatives of India Ltd (NACOF) reported a revenue of Rs 2,456 crore and a net profit of Rs 14.89 crore for the financial year 2025-26 at its annual general meeting (AGM) on Saturday.The federation also declared a 12 per cent dividend for its member societies. NACOF said it had operated without government funding and continued to comply with the standards and regulatory requirements of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) and other regulatory bodies.The AGM was attended by cooperative sector representatives, policymakers, former bureaucrats and political representatives, including NACOF Vice Chairperson Ranjeet Singh, former Tamil Nadu chief secretary Rajiv Ranjan, retired IAS officer and former Director General of the National Productivity Council Sundeep Nayak, former Jharkhand chief secretary Rajbala Verma and former NAFED managing director SK Chadha.NCUI Director and former Sahakar Bharati president D.N. Thakur, Dataganj MLA Rajeev Kumar Singh, Mirzapur MLA Rinky Koal, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP from Shirdi Bhau Saheb Rajaram Wakchaure, IFFCO Vice President Balvir Singh and NCUI Director Sunil Khatri were also present.NACOF said it is exploring partnerships with cooperative systems and farming organisations in Bangladesh, Iran, Russia and Chile, along with opportunities in Dubai and other international markets.The federation said it plans to use its cooperative network to establish business relationships and create opportunities for Indian cooperatives overseas. It has also invited member cooperatives across the country to identify new domestic business opportunities and explore expansion into international markets.A NACOF spokesperson said the federation's financial performance showed that a cooperative federation could operate independently and remain profitable without relying on government funds.NACOF said it would focus on turning cooperative agreements into actual business activity, rather than limiting partnerships to agreements and proposals.The federation said it was looking for individuals and member institutions that could implement business ideas and projects. Member cooperatives interested in joint ventures, expanding retail or procurement operations, or developing new value-chain connections have been invited to approach the NACOF head office.NACOF is a multi-state cooperative society registered under the Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India. It is engaged in the procurement, processing and distribution of agricultural commodities and related products and operates 25 branches across India.
Article Summary: National Federation of Farmers' Procurement, Processing & Retailing Cooperatives of India Ltd (NACOF) reported a revenue of Rs 2,456 crore and a net profit of Rs 14.89 crore for the financial year 2025-26. NACOF said it had operated without government funding and continued to comply with the standards and regulatory requirements of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies.

Article Title: Why FIIs may not return to Indian stocks even after AI boom fades
Article Text:
FIIs unlikely to return in large numbers without new growth engines in India: Bernstein

Foreign investors may continue to remain cautious on Indian stocks even after the artificial intelligence (AI) trade peaks, brokerage Bernstein said. It said foreign investors are unlikely to return in large numbers unless India is able to build industries and companies that can compete globally, making this a key factor for a sustained recovery in foreign investment.Bernstein expects foreign institutional investor (FII) flows to stay flat to slightly positive over the next 12 months. However, it said this would mainly show that some of the recent pressures on foreign investors have eased, rather than a major improvement in the factors that drive their long-term investment decisions.“We do not believe FIIs will return in large numbers even after the AI trade peaks,” the brokerage said.For foreign investors to return in a sustained way, India will need to create “new engines of competitiveness, innovation, and global relevance”, Bernstein said.The brokerage said India needs to show stronger capabilities in areas such as advanced semiconductor manufacturing, batteries and energy storage, and energy self-sufficiency.It also needs businesses that can win a meaningful share of global markets, Bernstein said.There are some early signs of this in sectors such as space, defence, semiconductors and deep-tech. However, most of these sectors are still too small to have a major impact on global investment decisions, it said.The comments come after a sharp change in foreign investment flows into Indian equities. FIIs have pulled out USD 40 billion from Indian stocks over the last two years.Over the past 24 months, FIIs recorded combined outflows of USD 56.3 billion. This compares with inflows of USD 38.6 billion in the 24 months before that.Bernstein said the link between India’s economic growth and FII flows has weakened. The earlier link between the interest-rate difference between India and the US and FII flows has also faded.Foreign investors are now paying more attention to currency movements, relative valuations and changes in expected earnings, the brokerage said.The rupee has become an important factor in FII flows. Bernstein said the correlation between FII flows and the currency has risen above 70% in recent years.This may mean that a weaker rupee is reducing the returns foreign investors get when their investments are measured in US dollar terms, it said.High valuations have emerged as another factor.Bernstein said its analysis showed that rising relative valuations have gone along with weaker FII flows in recent years, making it harder to attract foreign capital.The brokerage expects FII flows to remain flat to modestly positive over the next 12 months. But it said this would mainly reflect an easing of recent headwinds and not a major improvement in the factors that drive long-term foreign investment.For a sustained return of foreign capital, Bernstein said India will need to create a new generation of globally competitive companies and build new sources of competitiveness, innovation and global relevance.
Article Summary: Bernstein expects foreign institutional investor (FII) flows to stay flat to slightly positive over the next 12 months. It said this would mainly show that some of the recent pressures on foreign investors have eased, rather than a major improvement in the factors that drive their long-term investment decisions.

Article Title: Big dollar inflows, little boost for rupee: Why the currency may stay near Rs 96 in near term
Article Text:
Where is rupee headed in near term?

After suffering multiple lows over the year, rupee may now see some stability against the US dollar. The currency is likely to remain in the Rs 94.5-96 per dollar range in the near term, despite sizeable dollar inflows through FCNR deposits and external commercial borrowings (ECBs), according to a Bank of Baroda research report.The report said the inflows have largely gone into the Reserve Bank of India's reserves instead of entering the market. This has limited the extent to which the additional dollar supply could have translated into appreciation in rupee.“In the current situation a range of Rs 94.5-96 looks likely in the near term,” the report said. It added that sharp appreciation of the rupee, which could theoretically have followed the increase in dollar inflows, has been limited as the inflows “have not been infused into the market but added to reserves.”The report's analysis suggests that the exchange rate cannot be explained by dollar flows or any other individual factor in isolation. Rupee movements have been shaped by a combination of fundamentals, intervention by the RBI and market sentiment.The domestic currency has lost around 28 per cent since January 2022. The rupee's average exchange rate moved from Rs 74.44 per dollar in January 2022 to Rs 95.47 in August 2026.Other Asian currencies also weakened during this period, although to varying degrees. The yen depreciated by 38 per cent, while the Indonesian rupiah and South Korean won fell 24 per cent and 17 per cent, respectively. In comparison, the dollar gained 2.4 per cent against the euro.To assess what has been driving these movements, the Bank of Baroda report examined monthly currency data between January 2022 and June 2026. Its analysis covered changes in foreign exchange reserves, RBI operations in spot and forward markets, FPI flows and movements in the dollar-euro exchange rate.RBI intervention emerged as one of the variables with a significant relationship with rupee movements. The relationship was stronger when spot and forward interventions were considered together. Their combined explanatory power stood at 34 per cent, against 25 per cent for spot intervention alone and 19 per cent for forward operations alone.The report said this finding suggests that the RBI's use of both spot and forward operations together could be more effective in managing the currency.Forex reserves, on the other hand, had a relatively limited explanatory power of 18 per cent. The report said this indicates that even a sharp rise in reserves following dollar inflows does not necessarily produce a major movement in the exchange rate.FPI flows also showed a significant relationship with the rupee when examined separately. However, that significance disappeared once the other variables were considered alongside FPI flows.“The factors driving the exchange rate are through multiple routes and separating them statistically does not reveal any dominant variable,” the report said.The analysis found that the variables studied explained no more than 40 per cent of the variation in the rupee. A substantial portion of the movement remained outside what the analysis could capture.The report attributed much of this unexplained component to sentiment, including the timing of dollar purchases by importers and exporters and the flow of remittances.The findings therefore point to a currency market where movements are influenced through several channels rather than being driven by one dominant variable. Against this backdrop, the report expects the rupee to remain within the Rs 94.5-96 per dollar range in the near term.
Article Summary: Rupee is likely to remain in the Rs 94.5-96 per dollar range in the near term, according to a Bank of Baroda research report. The report said the inflows have largely gone into the Reserve Bank of India's reserves instead of entering the market.

Article Title: ‘40-year skill shelf life is over’: WorldSkills chief on AI-era jobs
Article Text:
Hourant's WorldSkills journey began in 2009 as CEO of WorldSkills Belgium

SHANGHAI: Learn a skill, get a job and rely on it for the next 40 years. That model of working life is over. Artificial intelligence may wipe out some entry-level work, but the bigger challenge is not to predict which jobs will disappear — it is to keep workers learning throughout their lives, WorldSkills president and chair Francis Hourant said, arguing that “human skills” must remain at the centre of the AI revolution.Speaking to The Times of India at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, Hourant said the pace of AI made even a 10- or 20-year forecast of jobs difficult. “We don’t know what we need in two years, in five years, in ten years,” he said, arguing that lifelong learning was no longer a choice.His advice to young people entering the workforce was simple: when discussing a new job, don’t only ask about salary and benefits — ask the employer what its plan is for your training. Without continuously acquiring new skills, he said, workers may find it difficult even to move between jobs or roles within the same company.WorldSkills members, Hourant said, have already adopted an AI policy that will evolve every year. The organisation will now examine how AI can be incorporated into its occupational standards, competition projects and assessment systems.But he cautioned against seeing AI as a substitute for people.“Human skills first,” he said, recalling companies that had chosen to retrain workers instead of replacing them. In one case, he said, a large company retrained 8,000 employees so they could move from simply selling products to becoming advisers to customers — and ended up improving business.The same principle, he said, should guide the use of robotics. The challenge is to decide “where is the right place for the robot and where is the right place for the human”. Automation, he suggested, could take over some of the most difficult or undesirable work, while people move into roles demanding judgement, creativity and human interaction.Hourant also underlined the role of international skills competitions as a benchmark for education systems. He cited the example of a Belgian expert who returned from a WorldSkills competition and told his training centre that teaching methods, equipment and investment had to change if it wanted to match international standards.Finland, he said, routinely brings experts together after competitions to share what they have learnt, and that feedback can even lead to changes in curricula.International mobility will add another layer to the challenge. Countries whose workers seek jobs abroad, Hourant said, can benefit not only from remittances but also from skills, training and technology flowing back home.On India, Hourant avoided a detailed assessment, saying he did not know the system closely enough. But he said India was strongly associated in Europe with technology, particularly IT, and cited European companies recruiting talent from the country.
Article Summary: Francis Hourant is the president and chair of WorldSkills. He said the pace of AI made even a 10- or 20-year forecast of jobs difficult. Without continuously acquiring new skills, workers may find it difficult even to move between jobs or roles within the same company.

Article Title: Her employer deducted Rs 3.91 lakh TDS but failed to deposit it; Mumbai IT professional got just Rs 79,030 credit and faced Rs 3.36 lakh demand, ITAT gives relief
Article Text:
As the deducted amount was not deposited, the complete TDS credit did not appear in her Form 26AS. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why ITAT Mumbai ruled in taxpayer’s favour

Lessons for employees

Your employer cuts Tax Deducted At source or TDS from your salary, but doesn’t deposit it. You get a tax demand notice. What do you do?A Mumbai-based IT professional faced this very situation when she received a tax demand of Rs 3.36 lakh, even though she had claimed Rs 3.91 lakh as TDS credit in her income tax return (ITR).For Assessment Year 2019-20, the woman reported an income of Rs 18.41 lakh in her ITR and claimed credit for Rs 3.91 lakh in TDS. However, she was given credit for only Rs 79,030, resulting in a tax demand of Rs 3.36 lakh.The reason was that her employer, an IT services company, had deducted TDS from her salary but had not deposited the amount with the government.She approached the Centralised Processing Centre (CPC) for rectification on several occasions, but her efforts did not resolve the issue.She subsequently filed a first appeal, which was rejected on the ground that it was time-barred. She then challenged the matter before the income tax appellate tribunal (ITAT), where she eventually got relief.The ITAT Mumbai observed that the woman had not received credit for the entire TDS amount because her employer had deducted tax from her salary but failed to remit it to the revenue.As the deducted amount was not deposited, the complete TDS credit did not appear in her Form 26AS.This led to the denial of her Rs 3.91 lakh TDS claim.She, however, produced several documents to establish that the tax had actually been deducted from her salary by her employer. These included her salary slips, Form 16, bank statements and other supporting records.After considering the documents and referring to recent rulings of the Supreme Court and a High Court, the tribunal held that an employee cannot be made liable for a tax demand where the employer has deducted tax at source from the employee’s salary income but failed to deposit the deducted amount with the government.The Rs 3.36 lakh tax demand will therefore also be nullified once the Assessing Officer verifies her claim of Rs 3.91 lakh in TDS and grants her the full credit, according to an ET report.In this case, the taxpayer succeeded because she was able to establish that TDS had actually been deducted from her salary.A taxpayer who can demonstrate that TDS was deducted, using documents such as Form 16 and salary slips, can rely on Section 205 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. In such a case, the Department cannot seek to recover the same tax from the employee.Once the TDS credit is allowed, the Rs 3.36 lakh tax demand will effectively stand nullified.Raghav Bajaj, Partner, Khaitan & Co says that the ITAT Mumbai ruling reinforces an important safeguard: where salary tax has demonstrably been withheld by an employer, the taxpayer employee should not bear the consequences of the employer’s failure to remit it.Section 205 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (corresponding to section 401 of Income-tax Act, 2025) draws a bright line: once tax is deducted, the obligation to remit it falls on the deductor, not the deductee.“By directing verification and grant of credit, the Tribunal recognises the evidentiary value of Form 16, salary records and banking trails. For taxpayers and practitioners, the implications are both reassuring and instructive,” he tells TOI.On the dispute resolution front, this decision makes clear that automated CPC processing under Section 143(1) - which matches TDS claims against Form 26AS - cannot be the final word where genuine deductions have occurred.“A mismatch in Form 26AS, standing alone, does not extinguish a legitimate TDS credit,” he says.According to Kuldip Kumar, Partner at Mainstay Tax Advisors LLP, the decision of the Mumbai ITAT is a useful reiteration of an important principle relating to TDS credit.There have been several other judgments of different Benches of the ITAT and various High Courts that have favoured the assessee in this regard.“The legal position is now strongly supported by a consistent line of judicial decisions that, where tax has actually been deducted at source but has not been deposited by the deductor, the assessee should not be denied the corresponding TDS credit or be made liable to pay the same tax again, provided the assessee is able to establish that the tax was in fact deducted,” Kumar tells TOI.Importantly, Kumar notes that this principle is not confined to tax deducted from salary. It can also apply to TDS deducted from other domestic payments, including contractor or professional fees, rent, interest, dividend and similar payments.In relation to their financial affairs, it is important for taxpayers to maintain proper documentation to establish that TDS was actually deducted.According to Kumar, for salaried taxpayers, this could include salary slips, employment letters and bank statements evidencing receipt of the net salary. In the case of other payments, copies of invoices, contracts or agreements, payment advice, ledger accounts and bank statements showing receipt of the net amount could serve as supporting evidence.It is also advisable to review Form 26AS/AIS periodically and reconcile the TDS reflected therein with the TDS actually deducted. Where a deduction is not reflected, the taxpayer should, where possible, promptly write to the employer or payer and request confirmation and correction. Such contemporaneous correspondence can also become important corroborative evidence if the deductor subsequently fails to deposit the TDS or file the relevant TDS statement.“Given the increasing reliance on electronic processing, a TDS mismatch may result in an automated demand being raised when the TDS claimed in the return is not reflected in Form 26AS/AIS. In such circumstances, the taxpayer should promptly seek rectification with the CPC / jurisdictional Assessing Officer with appropriate documentary evidence and seek grant of the TDS credit and consequential rectification of the demand,” Kuldip Kumar says.
Article Summary: Mumbai-based IT professional received a tax demand of Rs 3.36 lakh. She had claimed Rs 3,91 lakh as TDS credit in her income tax return (ITR) However, she was given credit for only Rs 79,030. Article Title: Asian Games 2026: What Indian medallists can earn in cash rewards, government jobs and state incentives
Article Text:
India's kabaddi players pose during the presentation ceremony. (PTI Photo)

How much does an individual medallist receive?

Competition Gold Silver Bronze Olympic Games Rs 75 lakh Rs 50 lakh Rs 30 lakh Asian Games Rs 30 lakh Rs 20 lakh Rs 10 lakh Commonwealth Games Rs 30 lakh Rs 20 lakh Rs 10 lakh

Team medals: the calculation changes

Multiple medals and the highest-award rule

Can Asian Games medallists get government jobs?

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the cash awards for Asian Games medal winners? They are fair and motivating. They should be increased. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

State incentives can add another layer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s medal winners at the Asian Games 2026 could return home with more than a place on the podium. Along with national recognition, athletes who win gold, silver or bronze are eligible for cash awards under a central government scheme. They may also qualify for sports-quota jobs and additional incentives announced by their respective state governments.The central cash awards are laid out in the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports’ “Special Awards to Medal Winners in International Sports Events and their Coaches” scheme. The scheme, first introduced in 1986, has been revised over time, with the stated aim of rewarding sporting achievement, encouraging higher performance and inspiring young people to take up sports.For an individual Asian Games medal, the listed central award is Rs 30 lakh for gold, Rs 20 lakh for silver and Rs 10 lakh for bronze. These are the base figures: the amount for a team medal depends on the size of the team and the scheme’s rules for calculating and distributing awards.Under the central scheme, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games medal awards are the same. Olympic medal awards are higher.The same corresponding award amounts apply to Para Games medal winners.The cash incentive is subject to the eligibility criteria and conditions prescribed by the government.That means an Indian athlete who wins an individual gold in Aichi-Nagoya could be eligible for a central award of Rs 30 lakh. A silver medallist’s listed award is Rs 20 lakh, while a bronze medallist’s is Rs 10 lakh.For team events, the scheme determines the award using the number of athletes in the team on the ground. The multiplier is applied to the corresponding individual-event award for the competition, medal and category.A team of two receives 1.5 times the corresponding award; a team of three or four receives twice the award; a team of five to 10 receives three times the award; and a team with more than 10 members receives five times the award. The resulting amount is shared equally among the team members, with a condition that no member receives less than 50% of the corresponding individual-event award.The scheme defines team events as competitions in which athletes compete collectively, and says incentives are awarded to all team members, including bench or reserve players, in accordance with the international standards applicable to each sport. It also provides that, in specified sports disciplines, each team member’s cash incentive is 75% of the incentive amount applicable to the corresponding individual event, based on the medal, level and participation category.These provisions mean that a team medal cannot simply be treated as the same flat award for every athlete. The final amount depends on the event’s classification, team strength and applicable scheme provisions.The scheme also addresses athletes who win more than one medal at an international event. As a general rule, a sportsperson who wins multiple medals in individual or team categories is eligible for the cash incentive only for the highest-ranking medal won at that event.There is an important exception for the Olympic Games, Paralympic Games, Asian Games and Para-Asian Games: athletes who win multiple medals in individual or team categories may be eligible for the cash incentive for each medal, subject to the scheme’s terms and conditions.For an Asian Games athlete who wins more than one medal, therefore, the central award may be calculated medal by medal rather than being limited to the single highest finish. The precise amount still depends on whether the medals were won individually or as part of a team, and on the applicable team-event rules.The figures and provisions above are from the Department of Sports, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports circular dated January 31, 2025, as provided in the scheme details.Cash awards are only one part of the potential support available to medal winners. Athletes who have represented India in recognised international competitions, including the Asian Games, may also be considered for recruitment under sports-quota provisions.At the central level, recruitment of meritorious sportspersons is governed by Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) instructions and related office memorandums. The central framework generally provides for appointment to Group C and erstwhile Group D posts, subject to eligibility, recruitment rules and the specific terms in force. It does not establish a general entitlement for every medal winner to receive a Group A or Group B post.A medal does not, by itself, mean that a job is automatically granted. Athletes must meet the relevant conditions, and appointments depend on the applicable recruitment process and rules. Serving government employees may also be covered by separate provisions, including certain out-of-turn promotion or incentive arrangements, where permitted.The amount an athlete may receive after the Games can vary further because state governments frame their own sports policies and service rules. Some states offer additional cash awards, employment opportunities or other incentives to athletes from their state who win medals at major international competitions.As a result, two Indian athletes who win the same medal at the Asian Games may be eligible for different overall benefits depending on their state’s policy and their individual circumstances. State incentives are not uniform across India, and any announced reward or job offer must be checked against the specific state’s policy, eligibility conditions and formal government orders.For athletes and families assessing what a medal could mean financially, the key distinction is between the central scheme’s published cash award and any separate state-level benefit. The central award schedule gives a clear starting point – Rs 30 lakh, Rs 20 lakh and Rs 10 lakh for individual Asian Games gold, silver and bronze – but the final package may depend on team-event calculations, multiple-medal provisions, state rules and eligibility for recruitment or other incentives.
Article Summary: India's medal winners at the Asian Games 2026 could return home with more than a place on the podium. Along with national recognition, athletes who win gold, silver or bronze are eligible for cash awards under a central government scheme. They may also qualify for sports-quota jobs and additional incentives announced by their respective state governments.

Article Title: Oil prices slide 2% as US-Iran seek path out of war, Saudi supply fears persist
Article Text:
Crude prices climbed as prolonged Iran tensions and disrupted Strait of Hormuz flows heightened concerns over Middle East oil supplies and refined-fuel availability.

Oil prices fell over 2% as markets weighed growing hopes of a US-Iran truce against fresh concerns over oil supplies from Saudi Arabia. Talk of a possible US ban on diesel exports also added pressure, widening the gap between US and global crude benchmarks.Brent crude fell $2.28, or 2.14%, to $104.30 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $2.20, or 2.33%, to $92.41. The moves left Brent up less than 1% over the week, while WTI was down about 8%.The latest decline came as US and Iranian negotiators in New York explored a phased route out of the war. According to sources close to the talks, the proposed path would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz in return for Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran.Iran, however, has indicated that the talks would not mean a change in its position on its nuclear programme. "Iran, however, said it will ⁠show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the US accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including lifting a US naval blockade on Iranian ports," a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.The Strait of Hormuz remains a key focus for oil markets, with crude flows out of the waterway reaching 33.7 million barrels in the week starting September 20, according to preliminary ship-tracking data from Kpler.The figure kept exports roughly in line with the previous week's levels.Before the Middle East conflict began, about 20% of the world's oil supplies moved through the strait.US discussions around a possible ban on diesel exports have emerged as another factor influencing crude prices. The prospect is widening the spread between US crude futures and the global Brent benchmark, indicating that markets expect US refiners to process less crude if they are unable to export their diesel output.The Brent premium over WTI rose to its highest level since May for a third consecutive day.
